rows.text: Thoth Tarot – Planetary Dignities & Properties
Golden Dawn / Crowley attributions (Book of Thoth, Liber 777). Classical seven planets + lunar nodes; outer planets per Crowley's elemental trumps.

The user's own reference sheet "Thoth Tarot – Planetary Dignities & Properties" (source/Thoth_Planetary_Dignities.pdf, 3 pages, 7 sections). It is the authority: every value below is copied from it verbatim, except the keys listed in "derived".
Crowley, The Book of Thoth (1944); Liber 777; Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos (classical dignities, nodal exaltations); Golden Dawn Book T.

Conventions. null = the sheet prints '—' (nothing / not given). List values are the sheet's comma lists split at ', ' (joined with ', ' they give the cell back exactly, capitals as printed). Cells that wrap onto two lines in the PDF are re-joined. Section 5 prints the Atu as 'XXI Universe', which is atu + ' ' + card here (the nodes' shared cell is atuNote). The two nodes share one row in sections 5 and 6 ('Dragon's Head / Tail', 'Nodes'); that row is copied to both node entries. Section 1's 'Ruler' column, section 3's reading-key 'Ruler', section 2's 'Domicile' and section 7's 'Rules' are the same dignity. Checked against the sheet text and journal.html by check_dignities.py.

Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius have no classical exaltation (later astrologers use Pluto/Uranus/Neptune; Crowley does not).
Modern rulers Uranus/Neptune/Pluto are not used in this scheme.
Nodes exalted in Gemini/Sagittarius per Ptolemaic tradition.
Fall = exalted planet of the opposite sign; detriment = ruler of the opposite sign.

Cross-reference: a planetary card beside a zodiacal card it rules or is exalted in strengthens both (Empress + Adjustment; Universe + Adjustment). Beside a sign where it is in detriment or fall it is weakened (Tower + Adjustment = Mars in Libra). The same key reads the Minor Arcana decans (each 2–10 is a planet in a sign).
a planetary card beside a zodiacal card it rules or is exalted in strengthens both (Empress + Adjustment; Universe + Adjustment).
Beside a sign where it is in detriment or fall it is weakened (Tower + Adjustment = Mars in Libra).
The same key reads the Minor Arcana decans (each 2–10 is a planet in a sign).
Colors are the King (Atziluth) scale from 777; the Thoth cards are painted mostly from it.
Outer-planet sephiroth are not fixed in 777 – later conventions only.

Method in a spread: (1) identify the card's sign or planet; (2) read the ruler row for its native mode and the exaltation row for its peak; (3) check neighbors – a planetary card next to a sign it rules/exalts in reinforces; next to a sign of detriment/fall it undermines; (4) apply the same to Minor decans.

No internal inconsistency found in the sheet. Sections 1, 2 and 7 agree sign by sign and planet by planet; every detriment is the ruler of the opposite sign and every fall the exalted planet of the opposite sign; exactly Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius lack an exaltation; no modern planet holds a dignity; section 5's Atus and letters agree with sections 2–3 and the nodes' 'Exalted in VI / XIV' with section 1; sections 1–3 cover the 22 Atus once each; the reading notes' claims, the three cross-reference examples, the kamea sums and the ages of life all check out (check_dignities.py, 2026-09-29).

The nodes share one row in section 5 ('Dragon's Head / Tail': only the Atu cell is filled, 'Exalted in VI / XIV') and in section 6 ('Nodes': '18.6 yr (retrograde)', 'Eclipse points'); both node entries carry that row.
Section 4 names the nodes 'Dragon's Head (N. Node)' and 'Dragon's Tail (S. Node)'; sections 1 and 7 say 'Dragon's Head' / 'Dragon's Tail'. Stored as planet + also.

The sheet gives the nodes no domicile or detriment (section 7: '—') and Uranus, Neptune, Pluto no dignities at all (modern rulers are not used): those fields are null. Planets have no element on the sheet except the three outer planets (section 3).

Every reading note in section 1 is written from its sign's ruler + exaltation (the column says so) and names them by keyword: Aries 'drive … clarity' (Mars, Sun), Taurus 'Beauty … instinct' (Venus, Moon), Gemini 'Analysis … fated union; eclipse' (Analysis = Mercury's 'Mind'; 'fated' = Dragon's Head 'fated gain'; 'eclipse' = the nodes' 'Eclipse points'), Cancer 'grace' (Jupiter), Leo 'the Sun', Virgo 'Mind … at its height' (Mercury twice), Libra 'Harmony … law' (Venus, Saturn), Scorpio 'Severance … Moon's fall' (Mars; fall Moon), Sagittarius 'expansion and release' (Jupiter, Dragon's Tail), Capricorn 'structure … force' (Saturn, Mars), Aquarius 'structure' (Saturn), Pisces 'love exalted; mind (Mercury) doubly lost' (Venus; Mercury detriment and fall). Never show a sign's note in a question that asks for that sign's dignities. Several notes also point to the sign's own Thoth card: Gemini 'Solve … marriage of Sol and Luna' (VI Lovers, the Royal Marriage), Sagittarius 'Coagula' (XIV Art), Libra '(Maat)' (VIII Adjustment), Aquarius '(Nuit)' (XVII Star), Scorpio 'putrefaction' (XIII Death), Cancer 'Receptive vessel' (VII Chariot's Grail). Never show a sign's note in a question that asks for that sign's Atu or card either.

Some keywords name their card: Jupiter 'Fortune' (its card is Atu X Fortune), Uranus 'sudden insight (Fool's air)', Neptune 'compassion (Hanged Man's water)', Pluto 'regeneration (Aeon's fire)'. Some fields of one planet repeat another of its fields: Sun keyword 'Vitality' = Sun body 'vitality'; Mercury keyword 'speech' = Mercury body 'speech'; Mercury ill-dignified 'nerves' = Mercury body 'Nerves'. False friends that are NOT that planet's card (a card-name leak guard should not trip on them, and they make tempting distractors): Venus keyword 'art' (XIV Art is Sagittarius), Venus trade 'lovers' (VI Lovers is Gemini), Pluto principle 'Death/rebirth' (XIII Death is Scorpio); the nodes' temperament 'Like Jupiter' / 'Like Saturn' names another planet. '(modern)', '(later use)' and '(unsettled)' mark the outer planets, and the nodes' Atu cell 'Exalted in VI / XIV' states their exaltations.

Not one-to-one, so a reverse question has more than one right answer: nature 'Benefic (luminary)' = Sun, Moon; 'Modern' = Uranus, Neptune, Pluto; temperament 'Hot, dry' = Mars, Sun; 'Cold, moist' = Venus, Moon; sect 'Diurnal / masc.' = Saturn, Jupiter, Sun; 'Nocturnal / fem.' = Venus, Moon; the two nodes share cycle and body; keyword 'destruction' = Mars and Pluto (both ill-dignified); sephira 'Kether' = Neptune ('Kether (later use)') and Pluto ('Da'ath / Kether (unsettled)'); near-identical cells: colours 'Blue' (Moon) / 'Deep blue' (Neptune), 'Yellow' (Mercury) / 'Bright pale yellow' (Uranus), 'Orange' (Sun) / 'Scarlet' (Mars) / 'Glowing orange-scarlet' (Pluto); cycles '1 yr' (Sun) / '~1 yr (synodic 584 d)' (Venus) / '~1 yr (synodic 116 d)' (Mercury), '29.5 yr' (Saturn) / '… 29.5 d synodic' (Moon); body 'arterial blood' (Jupiter) / 'venous blood' (Mars); domicile and detriment are two signs each for Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury.

A sign row can name one planet twice: Virgo (Mercury is ruler and exalted) and Pisces (Mercury is detriment and fall). Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius have no exaltation, so Aquarius, Taurus, Leo (their opposites) have no fall.
'Moon' and 'Sun' are planets and card titles: Atu XVIII Moon is Pisces (the planet Moon's card is Atu II Priestess); Atu XIX Sun is the Sun's own card. Say 'Atu XVIII Moon' or 'the planet Moon'.
Magical Compass — directional attributions

Every entry carries its own source and a confidence (high / medium / low). Azimuth is degrees clockwise from true north; -1 means the direction is computed (a bearing to Boleskine) or there is no fixed quarter (the wandering princes). 'goetia' is the app's cross-reference to the Goetia tool, set only where the entry names that same numbered spirit. 'set' is the compass set it is drawn with (the content table compass_sets: one of its layer's chips, or a set of kings); 'adoration', on the Liber Resh entries, names the adoration it is.

Star Ruby: the 1913 wording is now confirmed from an OCR of the 1913 Wieland first edition (archive.org) and the O.T.O./Celephaïs e-text: roar ΧΑΟΣ (E), scream ΒΑΒΑΛΟΝ (N), say ΕΡΩΣ (W), bellow ΨΥΧΗ (S), going widdershins. The earlier doubt about 'say' vs 'whisper' is resolved. Thelemapedia's version is wrong and should not be used. The revision first appeared in Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), Appendix VI, not 1944: roar ΘΗΡΙΟΝ, say NUIT, whisper BABALON, bellow HADIT. The Celephaïs collation prints the last three in Roman capitals, not Greek.

Star Ruby guardians: the compass points are inferred. The text places the four powers relative to the body (before, behind, right, left) after the operator returns to the centre. They become E, W, S, N only if the operator faces East at that point.

Liber Samekh (new entries): Crowley's Point II notes explicitly put Air in the East, Fire in the South, Water in the West and Earth in the North, with the Adept circling astrally widdershins and making the sign of the Enterer each time he passes the 'Kiblah', the direction of Boleskine. Spirit (Section F) is invoked from the centre facing Boleskine. Confirmed on the magicianandexorcist.org mirror and by search snippets from hermetic.com and sacred-texts. MTP is a 1929 publication, so the notes here are paraphrase only; the barbarous names come from the ancient Greek magical papyrus.

Liber Reguli: the text names compass quarters (N, S, E, W in that order, turning to the left), but the whole rite is aimed at Boleskine. Rodney Orpheus's commentary reads this as making Boleskine the temple's 'East', as in Liber XV. The app could offer 'true quarters' and 'Boleskine = East' modes. The West pentagram names no zodiac sign ('whereby Water is invoked'), so 'Scorpio' was removed.

Boleskine coordinates: OS NGR NH 50847 22116 (Buildings at Risk Register) converts to WGS84 57.2653, -4.4748 (computed with OSGB36→WGS84 Helmert). Wikipedia gives 57.2653°N 4.4747°W, about 6 m apart. The footnote printed with Liber Reguli reads 'Latitude 57.14 N. Longitude 4.28 W.' That is probably degrees and minutes (57°14′N 4°28′W, about 3.6 km off); read as decimal degrees it is about 14 km off, so do not use it. Use the great-circle initial bearing. Wikipedia describes the house as halfway between Foyers and Inverfarigaig; it burned in 2015 and 2019 and reopened after restoration in April 2026.

Elemental quarters vary by system. GD, 777, LBRP, the grade rituals and Liber Samekh: Air E, Fire S, Water W, Earth N. Agrippa's Scale of Four (Bk II ch. 7, checked at esotericarchives): Fire E, Air W, Water N, Earth S, with Michael E, Raphael W, Gabriel N, Uriel S. Liber O Lesser Hexagram: Fire E, Earth S, Air W, Water N. Liber Reguli: Earth E, Fire S, Water W, Air N. A 'Fire East / Air South' swap of the LBRP scheme appears in no GD or Crowley primary text checked; the nearest real sources for Fire in the East are Agrippa and the Hexagram ritual.

Rulers and Kerubim: Agrippa pairs Cherub with Air, Ariel with Earth, the Eagle with Air and the Man with Water. Liber 777 col. LX and the GD reverse the rulers (Ariel = Air, Kerub = Earth). 777 col. XXXVIII lists both 'Eagle, Man' against Air, while the GD grade rituals use the Man's head for Air and the Eagle for Water.

Winds: the directions are confirmed in Agrippa Bk I ch. 6 (Notus S, Boreas N, Zephyrus W, Eurus E, 'called Apeliotes'). Some classical authors make Eurus the south-east wind. No GD paper pairs the winds with elements, so no element is attached to them.

Flashing colours: Air yellow/violet, Fire red/green and Water blue/orange are consistent. Earth is uncertain: Wikipedia, citing Regardie p. 479, gives black with green letters; others give black/white or the four Malkuth colours (777 col. XV: citrine, russet, olive and black). Only secondary citations were checked, hence medium/low.

Enochian: spellings vary between Dee, the GD papers and Crowley. The grade rituals as transcribed give Edelperna, Ra-agiosel, Ic Zod Heh Chal, EMPEH ARSEL GAIOL and EMOR DIAL HECTEGA. According to Wikipedia, Dee's own writings do not attribute the angels to the quadrants in this way; the element-to-quarter mapping of the four tablets (Air E, Fire S, Water W, Earth N) is the Golden Dawn's. EXARP, BITOM, HCOMA and NANTA are the tablets' lines on the Tablet of Union, used as Spirit names.

Supreme Ritual of the Pentagram: the names (YHVH Air, Elohim Fire, El Water, Adonai Earth; Eheieh for active Spirit, AGLA for passive) were checked only through secondary web copies. The 'Supreme' form as usually printed is thought to have been arranged by Regardie from Inner Order material, so it stays medium. Do not confuse it with the LBRP, which uses YHVH E, Adonai S, Eheieh W and AGLA N whatever the element.

Grade divine names: the Earth opening adores 'Adonai ha-Aretz, Adonai Melekh' but invokes with 'Adonai Melekh', so the entry now carries both. The Fire opening says 'Tetragrammaton Tzabaoth', i.e. YHVH Tzabaoth. Checked on the stichtingargus.nl grade-ritual transcriptions.

Sphinx powers: the app's 777.json col. L lists only Noscere (Air), Audere (Water) and Velle (Fire). Tacere for Earth is the standard fourth power but is not in the app's data, so the Earth entry's extra says so.
Neophyte: the candidate is led to the North, 'the place of greatest symbolic darkness', after the obligation, not at first entry; the Stolistes note was corrected.

Liber 777 col. CX (Sepher Yetzirah) is Crowley's mapping (Chesed Height, Geburah Depth, Tiphareth E, Netzach W, Hod S, Yesod N). Other Kabbalistic mappings of the six directions differ (e.g. Chesed South, Geburah North), so it stays medium.

Liber Resh assumes the Northern Hemisphere (face South at noon, North at midnight). Southern-Hemisphere practitioners often face the Sun (North at noon), so offer this as an option. Sunrise and sunset azimuths also swing far from due E/W with the seasons. The app's data/resh.json spells the god 'Khepra'; Liber Resh has 'Khephra'.

Checked against the 1904 printing itself (scan on Wikimedia Commons, File:The Book of the Goetia (Mathers-Crowley, 1904).djvu), not only the 2003 Celephaïs re-set. Observations (four kings) = p. 31, The Invocation of the King and its footnote = p. 43, Ye Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge = p. 59. The 1904 print reads 'AMAYMON, CORSON, ZIMIMAY or ZIMINIAR, and GÖAP'. GÖAP has the umlaut; only the re-set prints GOAP. Page numbers for spirits 1-36 are omitted because the re-set's pagination differs from the 1904 print by about one page.

The footnote to Amaimon in Crowley's Enochian 'Potent Invocatioun of Hys Kynge' (p. 59) reads 'Or Gaap, Paimon, Zodimay, as the case may be', and the line itself gives 'East, (South, West, North)'. Read in order, that is Amaimon East, Gaap South, Paimon West, Zodimay North. So the Goetia 1904 does contain a Gaap = South attribution, an order-matched reading of Crowley's footnote, which uses 'Gaap' where the Observations have GÖAP. Göap = South has two supports inside the 1904 edition, while Weyer puts Goap in the West. Corson = West rests only on list order, since p. 59 substitutes Paimon for the West. Spirit 33 Gäap is low confidence: his own entry makes Amaymon his King (East), but the footnote treats Gaap as the southern king.

Agrippa's Hebrew names: matched by the order of III.24 (kings E, S, W, N) they would give Samuel E, Azazel S, Azael W, Mahazuel N. Agrippa's own 'Scale of the number four' (II.7) puts Samael, Azazel, Azael and Mahazael in explicit columns with 'The East, The West, The North, The South' and with Oriens, Paymon, Egyn, Amaymon: Samael E, Azazel W, Azael N, Mahazael S. Mathers' 1904 footnote follows the II.7 order. Only Samael (East) agrees under both readings; the other three follow II.7 at low confidence, with the alternative given in extra.

Agrippa chapter number (added when the data was merged): the goetic research cites Occult Philosophy III.24 for the four evil kings (Urieus/Oriens, Amaymon, Paymon, Egin) and their Hebrew names, while the angelic research cites III.18 for the same passage (and III.24 for the four princes of angels over the winds). One of the two chapter references for the evil kings is probably wrong; check the text before quoting a chapter. The directions do not depend on it.

Theurgia-Goetia azimuths are the literal 32-point values of the manuscript's names: East by South 101.25, South by East 168.75, South by West 191.25, West by South 258.75, West by North 281.25, North by West 348.75, North by East 11.25, East by North 78.75. The Theurgia text only says to face 'that point of the compass' where the king has his mansion, and nothing in it spaces the kings evenly. The even spacing comes from Trithemius' 16 winds; each affected entry gives the Trithemian 16-wind azimuth in extra. All 16 directions were confirmed against both the section openings and the conjurations in Peterson's Sloane 3825 transcription. The only discrepancy is Cabariel: the heading gives no point, Sl. 2731 says 'west & by North', and the conjuration says 'North & by West' (kept at medium).

Dropped: 'Royne (≈ Viné) under Egyn'. In the Folger V.b.26 transcription, Royne is item 48 of the Office of Spirits (MS p. 78) with no king or quarter, and he is not among Egin's twelve chief spirits (MS pp. 83-84).

Book of Oberon (Folger V.b.26) at MS p. 73: Orience of the east, Paymon of the west, Amaymon of the south and Egine of the North. MS p. 74 says to turn to the South to receive Amaymon and to look to the North when calling Egyn, and pp. 81-84 repeat the kings with twelve chief spirits each (not entered as separate points). The Folger transcription is copyright 2015 (Peterson and Harms); only facts are used from it.

Sloane 3853 fol. 258r names four kings of the air: Oriens East, Paymon West, Amaymon South and Egim North. On the same page, Add. 36674 fol. 65r puts Scor, Algor and Sefon under Oriens (East), Partas and Gamor under Amamion (South), and Vmbra and Anaboth under Egin (North); these subordinates are not entered as separate points. Wikipedia says Sloane 3853 makes Leraje, Aim, Bune and Paymon kings of the N, S, E and W, citing a secondary edition; this does not appear in Peterson's transcription and was not included.

The kings' quarters vary widely by tradition. Amaymon is East in Weyer and in the Goetia (Observations, Invocation of the King, spirit 70, p. 59); South in Agrippa (II.7 and the kings' chapter), Oberon and Sloane 3853; and North in Liber 777 (by row). Paimon is West in Goetia spirit 9, the 1904 p. 59 footnote, Agrippa, Oberon and Sloane 3853; North ('Aquilonem versus') in Weyer's Latin, which Scot renders 'northwest'; and South in 777. Oriens is East everywhere. Egyn/Egin is North in Agrippa, Oberon and Sloane 3853, while 777 puts Ariton (Mathers' equivalent of Egyn) in the West.

Only 7 of the 72 Goetia spirits carry a direction in the 1904 text: 1, 2, 9, 13, 32, 33 and 70. For 32 and 33 it is derived from Amaymon; for 13 it is a wand gesture towards the South and East, plotted at SE 135°. Confirmed for 1-36 in source/research/crowley_1904_text.json and for 1-72 in the crowley field of data/lesserkey.json, where 37-72 were transcribed from the 1904 print. Decan-based directions for other spirits are modern and are not in the 1904 text.

Ritual facts: the 1904 Goetia says the triangle is to be placed toward the quarter the spirit belongs to. The footnote on p. 43 says the quarter the spirit is attributed to decides which of the four chief kings is invoked. The Theurgia-Goetia says to face the compass point of the king's mansion, and that for the 11 wandering princes the facing does not matter.

Pseudomonarchia daemonum first appeared in the 1577 (fifth) edition of Weyer's De praestigiis daemonum, not 1563. Its four-kings passage (Amoymon E, Gorson S, Zymymar N, Goap W) and the binding hours are in the closing section, which is Scot 1584 XV.3. The Latin wording could not be quoted directly; the directions are confirmed through Scot and secondary citations, and Scot's English is used in the entries.

The Heptameron's winds were verified in Turner's English (B. Rowe's transcription): Sunday North, Monday West ('the winde of the Moon'), Tuesday East, Wednesday Southwest, Thursday South, Friday West, Saturday Southwest. The Latin for Sunday (Boreas), Monday (Zephyrus) and Tuesday (Subsolanus) was confirmed in the Folger MS; the other Latin wind names come from T.S. 2002. The printed text calls these kings 'angels of the air', though they behave as fallen aerial spirits (the closing notes for each day call them 'Spirits of the Air', and some of their effects are malefic), so they are kept in both the goetic and the angelic lists.

When the Heptameron day begins: the Heptameron says that in every country and season the first hour of the day starts at sunrise. The compass therefore switches weekday at local sunrise (computed with h0 = -0.833°), not at midnight.

How the Heptameron places these beings: the King and his ministers are written in the four angles of the outermost circle. Standing in the circle, the operator first calls from the four parts the angels who govern the planets and days, then the angels who rule the air that day. So the listed wind is the Air Angels' governing wind, but the rite also places their names at all four angles. Wednesday and Thursday list only two ministers, and Friday lists four.

Thursday and Saturday have no angels for the four quarters. The text says no angels of the air are found above the fifth heaven, so on Thursday four short Latin prayers are said toward E/W/N/S, and Saturday reuses Thursday's prayers. Yet both days still name a King of the Air with ministers. This contradiction is in the text itself.

Heptameron text: Robert Turner's English (1655), from Benjamin Rowe's 2000 e-text, with the Sunday lists spot-checked against the 1655 page scans on Wikisource. Variant spellings in 'extra' come from Frater T.S.'s revision (Celephaïs Press, 2002), which follows the Latin of Agrippa's Opera c.1600. Peterson's edition could not be loaded in full, so spellings were not checked against Peterson. The separate entry 'Vel' was removed: 'Caluel. Vel. Laquel.' uses the Latin 'vel' = 'or', so Caluel and Laquel are probably one angel. Sunday East: Turner prints 'Gabriel', T.S. (from the Latin) reads 'Fabriel', so that entry is medium.

The four archangels are placed differently in each tradition. Agrippa III.24: Michael E, Raphael W, Gabriel N, Nariel/Uriel S (the II.7 table agrees by column). Golden Dawn LBRP (Liber O 1909; 777 col. LIX with quarters from col. LVII): Raphael E, Michael S, Gabriel W, Auriel N. Bamidbar Rabbah 2:10: Gabriel before (east), Michael right (south by Num. 2), Raphael with Ephraim (west), Uriel left (north). Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 4 names no compass points and is not entered. The app shows these as separate sets.

Agrippa's scale of four pairs the elements and quarters as Fire–East, Air–West, Water–North, Earth–South. Agrippa's rulers of the elements (Seraph, Cherub, Tharsis, Ariel) get a quarter only by sharing a column in the II.7 table, so they are medium. 777 col. LX swaps two of them: Ariel rules Air and Kerub rules Earth.

Enochian Watchtower Kings: the Golden Dawn attribution as printed in Liber Chanokh (1912) is Plate IV East/Air (BATAIVAH), Plate V West/Water (RAAGIOSL), Plate VI North/Earth (ICZHHCAL), Plate VII South/Fire (EDLPRNAA); the invocations spell them BATAIVAH, RAAGIOSEL, IC-ZOD-HEH-CAL and EDELPERNA. Dee's own orientation is disputed: every reading puts ORO in the East; enochian.blog (12 Dec 2025) gives ORO E, MOR S, MPH W, OIP N, while the same author (20 Jan 2026) and Stenwick (2014, Tabula Recensa) give ORO E, MPH S, OIP W, MOR N. Any 'Dee' orientation should be labelled disputed.

Elements on the Enochian tablets: most accounts say Dee's records do not give the tablets elements and that the Golden Dawn added them. The Vision of the Four Watchtowers (20 June 1584; A True & Faithful Relation, 1659, pp. 168ff, seen only through secondary quotations) describes the East cloth as blood-red, the South lily-white, the West dragon-skin green and the North a very dark hair colour.

777 col. LVIII 'Supreme Elemental Kings' (Tahoeloj, Thahebyobeaatan, Ohooohatan, Thahaaothahe) are placed by 777's own quarter column, as spelled in the app's 777.json. 777 does not explain where these names come from, so they are medium.

Left out on purpose: Revelation 7:1 (four unnamed angels holding the winds), 1 Enoch (no confirmed named list by direction), the Heptameron's angels of the day and of the seasons (no direction), Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 4 (positions around the Throne only), the Grimorium Verum (continents, not compass points) and Abramelin's sub-princes (no quarters).

Duplicates kept on purpose: the LBRP archangels and 777's rulers and angels of the elements appear in both the quarters and the angelic lists; the Heptameron kings of the air appear in both the goetic and the angelic lists; Agrippa's evil kings and princes of devils appear twice (the goetic variant set, and the angel-layer cross-reference stored here under goetic). The compass shows each set only when it is switched on.

Live placements are the app's computation, not textual attributions: the spirits and Shem angels of the rising decan are placed at the Ascendant's azimuth, and the decan pairing (from goetia.json) is a modern scheme, not in the 1904 Goetia.

Copyright: the Heptameron (Turner 1655), Agrippa (1651), the Goetia (1904), Liber O (1909), 777 (1909), Liber Resh (1911), Liber Chanokh (1912), the Book of Lies (1913) and A True & Faithful Relation (1659) are public domain. Magick in Theory and Practice (1929), the T.S. edition (2002), the Folger transcription (2015), Regardie's Golden Dawn and the modern blogs are used for names, directions and short paraphrase only.
Of the Dignities — Book T's rule for a card and its neighbours (elemental dignity)

Golden Dawn, "A Description of the Cards of the Tarot, with their Attributions; including a Method of Divination by their use" (Book T), The Equinox Vol. I No. 8 (September 1912), section "OF THE DIGNITIES", p. 206. Public domain.

Transcribed on 2026-09-29 from the original 1912 letterpress setting: page image and OCR text of https://archive.org/details/crowley-equinox_202110 (file "The Equinox Vol. 1, No. 8", leaf 236 = p. 206). The two agree word for word. "A CARD" is set in small capitals in print and is written "A card" in text. The section follows the table of majorities (pp. 205-206) and comes just before "A Method of Divination by the Tarot" (p. 207). This is the same printing that divination.json quotes for the card meanings.
OF THE DIGNITIES
A card is strong or weak, well dignified or ill dignified, according to the cards next to it on either side.
Cards of the same suit on either side strengthen it greatly, for good or evil according to their nature.
Cards of opposite natures on either side weaken it greatly, for either good or evil.
Swords are inimical to Pentacles.
Wands are inimical to Cups.
Swords are friendly with Cups and Wands.
Wands are friendly with Swords and Pentacles.
If a card fall between two others which are mutually contrary, it is not much affected by either.
Aces are always strong cards.
the table of majorities, row "A Majority of Aces" ("Strength generally. Aces are always strong cards."), p. 205 (leaf 235)
rules
suits
inimical
friendly

Everything except "text" and "majorityNote" is derived from the text. The rules are sentences 2, 3 and 8, split into a condition and an effect. "inimical" and "friendly" are sentences 4 to 7. "unstated" is the one pair of suits the text gives no relation for. The elements of the suits are the Golden Dawn / Liber 777 ones: Wands Fire, Cups Water, Swords Air, Pentacles (Thoth: Disks) Earth. In those elements, Fire and Water are contrary, and so are Air and Earth.

Suits only. The rule speaks of suits and says nothing about the Keys (trumps). The drills therefore use only the 56 suit cards: the Aces, the small cards 2-10 and the court cards. Liber 777 does give the Keys elements: a zodiacal Key's sign has one, and 0, XII and XX are Air, Water and Fire. But Book T never says the rule counts them, and the planetary Keys have no element at all.
Neighbours. "The cards next to it on either side" means the card just before it and the card just after it in the line. Only those two count, however long the spread is.

Settled cases only. The drills use only the three cases the text rules on. (1) Both neighbours are of the card's own suit: strengthened greatly. (2) Both neighbours are of the suit inimical to it ("opposite natures"): weakened greatly. (3) The two neighbours are inimical to each other (Wands with Cups, or Swords with Pentacles): not much affected by either. The text gives no ruling for any other pair of neighbours, for example the card's own suit beside a friendly suit, two Swords beside a Wand, or one inimical neighbour next to a friendly one, so these are never drilled. Two friendly neighbours that are contrary to each other (a Wand and a Cup beside a Sword) come under case (3).

Friendship. The text names the friends of Swords (Cups, Wands) and of Wands (Swords, Pentacles). It gives no relation between Cups and Pentacles, and it gives friendly neighbours no effect of their own.

Well and ill dignified. The first sentence pairs "strong" with "well dignified" and "weak" with "ill dignified". So a card its neighbours strengthen is read by its Book T meaning, and a card they weaken is read by its "if ill dignified" reading, where Book T gives one. In divination.json, 19 suit cards have one: every court card except the Queen of Cups, plus the Ten of Wands, Two of Cups, Eight of Swords and Six of Disks. The Ten of Wands is the only one that also has a "when well dignified" reading, and that reading is used for it. Book T adds that same-suit neighbours strengthen a card "for good or evil according to their nature".
Aces. Book T's table of majorities says "Aces are always strong cards". So no drill judges an Ace. Aces appear only as neighbours.

Essential dignity is a separate method. Reading a small card by the planet of its decan, or a planetary Key beside a zodiacal Key, comes from the user's sheet (dignities.json: crossRef, spreadMethod), not from Book T. The two methods are taught side by side and never mixed in one answer.

The Goetia's method is compulsion: conjurations, constraints, curses, seals worn as lamens, and the Brass Vessel. It does not prescribe offerings as a general rule. The exceptions are Belial ('must have Offerings, Sacrifices and Gifts presented unto him by the Exorcist, or else he will not give True Answers') and Paimon ('if thou callest this Spirit Paimon alone, thou must make him some offering'). Malphas is a warning: he receives sacrifices 'kindly and willingly' but will deceive the one who makes them. Beleth must be received courteously and done homage. Neighbouring grimoires go further: the Grand Grimoire's pact with Lucifuge Rofocale demands a coin each month, and the Grimoire of Pope Honorius involves sacrificing a black cock.

Modern practitioners broadly treat offerings as relationship-building or as payment for a completed task. Common offerings are incense, candles, alcohol, water, food (sweets, bread, honey, fruit), music, art, written praise, public thanks and charity. Aaron Leitch advises small offerings to attract a spirit and full payment only after results. He warns against paying unvetted or deceptive spirits up front (he cites Malphas). Many writers stress promising only what you can actually give. Blood offerings are controversial: some demonolatry currents use a few drops, while most Solomonic-leaning sources and sites like Goetic Impressions advise against them.

Classical sources say nothing on disposal. A common modern rule is to remove perishable food and drink after about a day, or once it has visibly 'been taken'. Then bury it, leave it at a crossroads or in nature (if it is biodegradable and safe for wildlife), pour liquids onto earth, or compost it, rather than throwing it in household trash. Candles and incense are usually left to burn out, with remains buried or discarded respectfully.

The Goetia itself says to observe the Moon's age: 'The best days be when the Moon Luna is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, or 14 days old... and no other days be profitable.' That is even days of the waxing moon, alongside the rank hours above. Modern practice adds the planetary day and planetary hour of the rank's planet (e.g. a King on Sunday in a Sun hour) and a waxing moon for constructive aims. Another modern option uses the Golden Dawn / 777 decan attributions, where spirits 1-36 are day spirits and 37-72 night spirits across the 36 decans; many practitioners work when the Sun is in the spirit's decan or 5-degree quinance.

Agrippa's planetary fumes include animal brains and blood, and Saturnian recipes include poisonous henbane, mandrake and black poppy. Treat these as historical data and do not burn or offer them. Quicksilver is toxic, so use electrum or plated metal for Presidents' seals. Alcohol, flame and incense safety apply. Rank-to-planet-to-day links beyond the metals are later inference, not stated outright in the Goetia.

"The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King. Translated into the English Tongue by a Dead Hand [S. L. MacGregor Mathers] ... The Whole Edited, Verified, Introduced and Commented by Aleister Crowley." Society for the Propagation of Religious Truth, Boleskine, Foyers, Inverness, 1904. This is the text of the Mathers/Crowley 1904 edition, but it comes from the Celephaïs Press re-set electronic edition of 2003 ("This re-set electronic edition prepared by Celephaïs Press ... 2003 E.V."), not from scans of the 1904 print. Page numbers in the source are 12-23 (spirits 1-36).

How the text was established: I compared two independent OCRs of the Celephaïs file and corrected clear OCR errors, e.g. "(i.)" to "(1.)", "io" to "10", "SlTRL" to "SITRI", "litthke" to "little", "1s" to "is", "Gdap" to "Gäap". Line-end hyphens were joined (for example "govern-/eth" became "governeth"). Words the source prints in small capitals are given in capitals (LUCIFER, LABAL, ABALIM, AMAYMON, BEALE, BOFRY). The triangle symbol after "triangle", which both OCRs read as "A", is given as Δ. Curly quotes and apostrophes were changed to straight ASCII ones. Footnote reference numbers were removed from the running text, and the footnotes are added at the end of each entry as [Note: ...], in the order they occur. "—ED." marks Crowley's notes, "—TRANS." marks Mathers' notes, and unmarked notes are the translator's.

Spelling slips that both OCRs show are kept exactly as in the source: "Spirt" (9), "courtesously" and "come into it. and" (13), "Seveteenth" (17), "Sontes" (18), "eppeareth" (22), "Sprit" and "life a Calf" (23), "(or Bim)" and "hegoverneth" (26), "giv-eth" (29), "party of that of Angels" (30), "there parts" and "invincibilitiy" (31; the second OCR reads "invincibilitty"), "He given the Ring" (32), "seventeeth" and "Stolas, or Stolas" (35-36), "ORder" (8), "SITRI—" with no full stop (12), and "(22.)—IPOS." I could not reach scans of the 1904 printing, so I could not check whether these slips are in the 1904 edition or were added in the 2003 re-set. A modern corrected retyping (archive.org "the-lesser-key-of-solomon-goetia") reads "Seventeenth", "like a Calf", "Stolos" and "courteously" in the same places. The seal images are not included.

It does not match the 1904 print in several places: 38 heading 'HALPHUS' where the print has HALPHAS; 45 'Things Past, Present and to Come' where the print has 'Things Present, Past, and to Come'; 46 'Bifrous' for Bifröus; 54 leaves out 'those' and reads 'Souls of the Deceased' for 'Souls Deceased'; 61 leaves out 'also Water into Wine'; 62 'Ualuc' for Ualac; 66 has 30 Legions where the print has 20; 69 'Decarbia' for Decarabia; 70 leaves out the sentence 'He governeth 26 Legions of Spirits.' The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King, translated by S. L. MacGregor Mathers ('a Dead Hand'), edited with annotations by Aleister Crowley. Society for the Propagation of Religious Truth, Boleskine, Foyers, Inverness, 1904. Transcribed from the scan of the original 1904 printing, printed pages 22-31. Transcription conventions: (1) Small capitals are rendered as full capitals. This covers the spirit names in each heading, LUCIFER and AMAYMON, and the footnote signatures ED. and TRANS. (2) Words broken by a hyphen at a line end are joined, e.g. Fur-calor becomes Furcalor. (3) Footnote markers keep the original per-page numbers as superscripts (¹ ² ³ ⁴), so a note can be ² when it is the second note on its page. The note text is appended to the end of the entry as [Note: n text]. The 1904 notes are by Mathers, unsigned or signed TRANS., and by Crowley, signed ED. (4) The printed triangle sign is given as Δ and the pentagram sign in 69 as ⛤. (5) Original spelling, capitalisation and punctuation are kept, including Phœnix, Räum, Viné, Bifröus, Caïm, Osé, 'steal Treasures out King's Houses', 'the Markis' and 'his Seal is thus.' The seal images themselves are printed on separate plates and are not included.

The 1904 text of all 72 spirits was transcribed from scans of the 1904 printing (Wikimedia Commons). Every listed difference was checked against the 1904 page images. The seals shown are de Laurence's 1916 plates.

THESE be the 72 Mighty Kings and Princes which King
Solomon Commanded into a Vessel of Brass, together with their Legions. Of whom BELIAL, BILETH, ASMODAY, and GAAP, were Chief. And it is to be noted that Solomon did this because of their pride, for he never declared other reason why he thus bound them. And when he had thus bound them up and sealed the Vessel, he by Divine Power did chase them all into a deep Lake or Hole in Babylon. And they of Babylon, wondering to see such a thing, they did then go wholly into the Lake, to break the Vessel open, expecting to find great store of Treasure therein. But when they had broken it open, out flew the Chief Spirits immediately, with their Legions following them; and they were all restored to their former places except BELIAL, who entered into a certain Image, and thence gave answers unto those who did offer Sacrifices unto him, and did worship the Image as their God, etc.

OBSERVATIONS.

FIRST, thou shalt know and observe the Moon’s Age for thy working. The best days be when the Moon Luna is 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, or 14 days old, as Solomon saith; and no other days be profitable. The Seals of the 72 Kings are to be made in Metals. The Chief Kings’ in Sol (Gold); Marquises’ in Luna (Silver); Dukes’ in Venus (Copper); Prelacies’ in Jupiter (Tin); Knights’ in Saturn (Lead); Presidents’ in Mercury (Mercury); Earls’ in Venus (Copper), and Luna (Silver), alike equal, etc.

THESE 72 Kings be under the Power of AMAYMON, CORSON, ZIMIMAY or ZIMINAIR, and GÖAP, who are the Four Great Kings ruling in the Four Quarters, or Cardinal Points,¹ viz.: East, West, North, and South, and are not

FOOTNOTE: 1 These four Great Kings are usually called Oriens, or Uriens, Paymon or Paymonia, Ariton or Egyn, and Amaymon or Amaimon. By the Rabbins they are frequently entitled: Samael, Azazel, Azäel, and Mahazael.
to be called forth except it be upon Great Occasions; but are to be Invocated and Commanded to send such or such a Spirit that is under their Power and Rule, as is shown in the following Invocations or Conjurations. And the Chief Kings may be bound from 9 till 12 o’clock at Noon, and from 3 till Sunset; Marquises may be bound from 3 in the afternoon till 9 at Night, and from 9 at Night till Sunrise; Dukes may be bound from Sunrise till Noonday in Clear Weather; Prelates may be bound any hour of the Day; Knights may from Dawning of Day till Sunrise, or from 4 o’clock till Sunset; Presidents may be bound any time, excepting Twilight, at Night, unless the King whom they are under be Invocated; and Counties or Earls any hour of the Day, so it be in Woods, or in any other places whither men resort not, or where no noise is, etc.

NOTE.—It will be remarked that several among the above Spirits possess two titles of different ranks; e.g., (45.) Viné is both King and Earl; (25.) Glasya-Labolas is both President and Earl, etc. "Prince" and "Prelate" are apparently used as interchangeable terms. Probably the Seals of Earls should be made of Iron, and those of Presidents in mixture either of Copper and Silver, or of Silver and Mercury; as otherwise the Metal of one Planet, Mars, is excluded from the List; the Metals attributed to the Seven Planets being: to Saturn, Lead; to Jupiter, Tin; to Mars, Iron; to the Sun, Gold; to Venus, Copper; to Mercury, Mercury and mixtures of Metals, and to Luna, Silver.

THE MAGICAL CIRCLE.

THIS is the Form of the Magical Circle of King Solomon, the which he made that he might preserve himself therein from the malice of these Evil Spirits. (See Frontispiece, Figure 153.) This Magical Circle is to be made 9 feet across, and the Divine Names are to be written around it, beginning at EHYEH, and ending at LEVANAH, Luna.

(Colours.—The space between the outer and inner circles, where the serpent is coiled, with the Hebrew names written along his body, is bright deep yellow. The square in the centre of the circle, where the word "Master" is written, is filled in with red. All names and letters are in black. In the Hexagrams the outer triangles where the letters A, D, O, N, A, I, appear are filled in with bright yellow, the centres, where the T-shaped crosses are, blue or green. In the Pentagrams outside the circle, the outer triangles where "Te, tra, gram, ma, ton," is written, are filled in bright yellow, and the centres with the T crosses written therein are red.¹)

THE MAGICAL TRIANGLE OF SOLOMON.

THIS is the Form of the Magical Triangle, into the which Solomon did command the Evil Spirits. It is to be made at 2 feet distance from the Magical Circle and it is 3 feet across. (See Frontispiece Figure 154.) Note
